children: Mubbadrah Investment has announced that it is leading a consortium of Omani and international companies, including Sustopia Capital, Vela Tech and O2 Global Energy, to develop a large-scale AI data centre in Oman, purpose-built for hyperscalers, with a planned capacity of up to 400MW. The initial investment is US$3bn with plans for project expansion in the future.

The announcement was made at a signing ceremony in London, attended by Nasser bin Khamis Al Jashmi, Chairman of Oman Tax Authority; Dr Liane Saunders, UK Ambassador to Oman; and representatives of the UK trade office. The project comes against the backdrop of the state visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik to the UK, reflecting the spirit of cooperation between the two countries.
The centre will host large-scale AI training and inference workloads, bringing together local and international expertise with global capital, technology and development capability.

Mubbadrah Investment, a leading investment group in Oman, leads the consortium of Omani and international companies. Sustopia Capital and Vela Tech are currently developing, designing and constructing about 20GW of AI data centre capacity around the world.

The US-based Crusoe, which specialises in AI infrastructure and cloud computing, has indicated interest as a potential off-taker for the project’s data centre capacity. The consortium expects to sign a confirmation of this interest in the next few weeks as the project develops.

The data centre will be powered by a blend of grid and renewable energy. In addition to power from the grid, O2 Global Energy will develop 400MW of solar generation with battery storage, strengthening the centre’s access to clean, reliable power.

“As an Omani investment group with a portfolio of more than 20 companies across oil and gas, hospitality, healthcare and other sectors, Mubbadrah Investment is proud to lead this consortium of Omani and international companies,” said Yasser Al Barami, CEO of Mubbadrah Investment.

He added, “Oman has the stability, the strategic location and the energy resources to become a regional home for AI infrastructure, and we are delighted to bring together partners with the capital, technology and experience to make that happen, creating lasting value and opportunities for Oman and its people.”

Nikhil Chouguley, CEO, Sustopia Capital, said that he was proud of Sustopia Capital’s growing role in developing the next generation of mission-critical digital infrastructure. “Through our 5GW data centre platform spanning Denmark, the US and the UK, we are building the foundations for the next era of AI, quantum computing and digital innovation. Our expansion into Oman is a strategic extension of this vision, positioning Sustopia at the intersection of the global AI infrastructure and energy transition.”

Yazan Faouri, Founder and CEO of O2 Global Energy, added that the company was excited to be a part of this development. “O2 Global Energy is active in several countries and brings 12 years of experience developing solar and renewable energy projects. As the founder of both O2 and H2 Global Energy, a leading green hydrogen and green ammonia developer in the MENA region, I look forward to delivering clean, reliable power for one of the region’s most important digital infrastructure projects.”
